kurz: Bread stays fresh longer when the starch firms up more slowly and the bread does not go mouldy.
bild_im_kopf: Like a clock you can slow down: acid, water and the right storage put the brakes on.
bedeutung: Stale means the starch has reorganised. More water in the dough, acid from sourdough, fat and proper storage slow this down.
was_passiert: [[sauerteig|Sourdough]] breads and breads with a lot of water stay fresh noticeably longer. In the fridge the starch firms up faster; in the freezer it holds still.
faustregeln: Bread bin or cloth rather than the fridge.
Whatever will not be eaten within two days: slice and freeze it.

praxis.text: A scald or cooked flour paste (tangzhong) in the dough binds extra water and keeps the [[krume|crumb]] soft for longer.
